curriculum.title: Devotion, Fellowship, Breaking Bread, and Prayer

core.big_idea: The earliest community was formed through apostolic teaching, shared life, breaking bread, prayer, and generosity.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic mission: Shared Life within the Church, Worship, and Mission cycle

claims.statement: Acts 2:42 names apostolic teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers as continuing practices of the Jerusalem believers.
Acts 2:43-47 describes generosity, shared meals, worship, favour, and daily growth in the community.
The passage is strong evidence for the formative practices of the earliest Jerusalem church, but by itself does not settle every later question about frequency or liturgical form.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present the inference as a direct quotation or explicit universal command.

claims.statement: Within this curriculum framework, Acts 2:42 contributes to the case that breaking bread belonged to the regular gathered life of the earliest church, while the weekly first-day frequency is established from a wider New Testament pattern rather than Acts 2 alone.
claims.interpretive_hinge: Acts 2 establishes continuing devotion to breaking bread; Acts 20:7 and 1 Corinthians 11 supply additional evidence used by this framework when reasoning about congregational practice and frequency.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that the earliest community was formed through apostolic teaching, shared life, breaking bread, prayer, and generosity.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The earliest community was formed through apostolic teaching, shared life, breaking bread, prayer, and generosity.
The lesson belongs in Apostolic mission.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Classify each major claim by evidence type.
State one credible interpretive limit or alternative before application.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.
